daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The KPK has raided immigration offices in Jakarta in connection with the ongoing corruption case involving former Deputy Minister of Immigration Silmy Karim, with searches conducted at both the South Jakarta and Central Jakarta immigration offices. The anti-corruption body also detained three suspects in a separate corruption case related to SPBU digitalization at a state-owned enterprise, while extending the detention of Muara Enim Regent Edison for 30 days. Additionally, the KPK revealed that the Regent of Kuansing has cut employee bonuses by up to 50 percent, and opened three new investigation orders in the expansion of the Banjarmasin tax corruption case.

  • The Central Jakarta District Court upheld Mardiono's leadership following the PPP's 10th National Congress, affirming the party's internal election results.
  • Non-parliamentary parties proposed that the electoral law limit factual verification to new parties only, seeking to ease requirements for established political organizations.
  • Partai Gema Bangsa urged lawmakers to retain the open proportional system in the upcoming electoral law revision.
  • The government extended work-from-home arrangements for civil servants to one day per week starting August 2026, with officials expressing optimism that the policy will modernize and improve bureaucratic efficiency.
  • The Home Affairs Minister stated that population data will serve as the foundation for digital public services across Indonesia.
  • An ANGGOTA DPRD from South Tangerang, Ahmad Andi Wibowo, died in an accident on the Cipali toll road.
  • President Prabowo reminded coal mining companies holding IUPK permits that they are obligated to implement downstream processing.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia strongly condemned Israeli attacks that are hindering the Gaza peace plan, with the Foreign Ministry issuing a formal statement criticizing actions that obstruct diplomatic efforts toward a ceasefire. The Ministry of Migrant Worker Protection held an audience with the Portuguese ambassador to discuss finalizing a memorandum of understanding on Indonesian migrant workers in Portugal. Meanwhile, Indonesian air force commanders urged pilots to sharpen combat skills in preparation for enhanced operational readiness.

  • A fishing boat from Ternate drifted at sea for 26 days before being rescued by a French vessel and evacuated to China.
  • The Indonesian Chamber of Commerce (Kadin) stated that Indonesia and Thailand can become global food security leaders through enhanced bilateral cooperation.

Other

The government removed five million underage accounts from social media platforms under its new digital child protection policy, a figure that exceeds TikTok Australia's achievements in similar enforcement. Six ministries teamed up to expand child protection efforts, while the government launched a national movement targeting a reduction in child violence and pledged that no violence should occur against children. The initiatives include plans to evaluate schools annually for child-friendly environments.

  • The Health Minister announced that lab results and medical records will soon be accessible like bank account information, with the SATUSEHAT app set to display complete health histories and AI analysis.
  • Indonesia identified 13,297 suspected leprosy cases through intensified nationwide screenings, while the Health Ministry found that 2.2 million teenagers have above-normal blood pressure.
  • The Basic Education Minister explained that the crisis in public elementary schools stems from oversupply and increasing preference for private schools.
  • The government offered incentives to Toyota to relocate production facilities to Indonesia as part of its automotive industry development strategy.
  • The Fisheries Ministry seized 92 illegal fishing vessels, saving an estimated Rp360 billion in potential losses to state revenues.
